identity.title: Mind Your Margin and Boundary: Are Your Distilled Datasets Truly Robust?

problem.claim: Dataset distillation seeks compact synthetic training sets that retain accuracy while providing robustness to adversarial attacks.

gap.claim: Existing methods either leave robustness uncontrolled or incur an accuracy–robustness trade-off by treating adversaries uniformly and not widening inter-class boundary separation.

contributions.claim: Introduces C²R, combining an attack-aware curriculum with a contrastive robustness objective.

Derives a perturbation score approximating each sample’s robust hinge to prioritize smallest-margin adversaries, alongside a class-balanced contrastive loss that promotes adversarial invariance and wider cross-class boundary separation.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish C²R by coupling robust-margin-driven curriculum selection with explicit contrastive boundary separation in dataset distillation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that experiments across CIFAR-10/100, Tiny-ImageNet, and multiple ImageNet-1K subsets under six attacks achieve the best robust accuracy among the compared methods.
The authors report a 2.8% average robust-accuracy improvement over prior robust dataset distillation methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Dataset distillation compresses training data, but conventional methods optimize clean accuracy without controlling robustness.
Prior robust approaches improve robustness but often weaken the accuracy–robustness trade-off because they overlook near-zero-margin adversaries and boundary separation.
C²R addresses these issues with an attack-aware curriculum based on perturbation scores and a class-balanced contrastive robustness loss.
Across several datasets and six attacks, the authors report leading robust accuracy and a 2.8% average gain over prior robust DD.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects the proposed curriculum directly to near-zero robust margins and connects the contrastive loss to attack-concentrated decision boundaries.

lessons.interpretation: A method claim is more informative when each component is tied to a specific failure mechanism.
lessons.application: For a robustness paper, map each design component to a measurable risk factor such as margin concentration or class-boundary separation.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the method has no clearly identified mechanism or when the target task is not margin- or boundary-based.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the six attacks, model architectures, training settings, clean-accuracy results, or statistical variability.
The reported “best” robust accuracy and 2.8% gain cannot be independently assessed from the abstract alone.
